text.title: Rails ActiveRecord Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules grounding the Rails ActiveRecord methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Query Objects MUST accept a relation in `initialize(relation = Model.all)`, chain methods returning `self`, and expose a terminal `results` method returning the relation (never an array).
rule.rationale: Returning the relation defers execution and allows further scoping at the controller level; `to_a` freezes the query and forfeits composability.

rule.statement: Filters MUST live in named scopes (`scope :active, -> { where(deleted_at: nil) }`), and any WHERE clause used at ≥2 call sites MUST be extracted into one. `default_scope` is forbidden.
rule.rationale: `default_scope` is invisible at every call site; debugging "missing data" wastes an hour per incident. Duplicated inline `where` drifts as the rule changes, while a named scope carries the business meaning and one place to edit.

rule.statement: Eager-loading MUST happen at the controller boundary via `.includes` / `.preload` / `.eager_load`. Views MUST NOT trigger relation accesses against un-loaded associations.
rule.rationale: View-triggered queries are invisible in code review; centralising at the controller makes query cost reviewable. Pick deliberately: `preload` issues a second query, `eager_load` a LEFT OUTER JOIN, and `includes` lets Rails choose — only `eager_load` lets you filter on the association.

rule.statement: Loops over > 1000 records MUST use `find_each` or `in_batches`. `Model.all.each` on growable tables is forbidden.
rule.rationale: `all.each` loads the full result set; `find_each` streams in batches and keeps memory constant.

rule.statement: Where clauses MUST use hash conditions or `where(...)` with placeholders. String interpolation into `where("name = '#{input}'")` is forbidden.
rule.rationale: String-interpolated WHERE clauses are SQL-injection vectors; AR placeholders are safe by default.

rule.statement: CI MUST run a N+1 gate (Prosopite or Bullet in CI mode). Specs that trigger an N+1 MUST fail.
rule.rationale: Without an automated gate, agents reintroduce N+1 within one sprint of the last fix.

rule.statement: Any sequence with ≥2 writes (`save` / `create!` / `update!` / `destroy`) MUST run inside `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do ... end`. `update_all` / `delete_all` MUST NOT be used for state-changing business logic.
rule.rationale: A mid-sequence failure otherwise leaves half-applied state that has to be reconciled by hand; `update_all` writes straight to SQL, skipping callbacks, validations and the audit trail.

rule.statement: A column holding a closed set of states MUST be an integer column declared with `enum status: { pending: 0, paid: 1, ... }`. Magic strings or bare integers in queries are forbidden.
rule.rationale: The enum generates scopes and predicate methods and makes a typo a NoMethodError at load time instead of a query that silently returns nothing.

rule.statement: Business logic MUST use `Time.current` / `Date.current`. `Time.now` and `Date.today` are forbidden; enforce with the `Rails/TimeZone` RuboCop cop.
rule.rationale: `Time.now` reads the server's zone rather than `config.time_zone`, so reports and scheduled work drift by whole hours the moment the host's zone differs.

rule.statement: An association whose count is rendered on a list or index page MUST declare `counter_cache: true` on the `belongs_to` side, with the matching `*_count` column added by migration and backfilled. Calling `.count` per row inside a loop is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Without it each rendered row issues its own `SELECT COUNT(*)`, which is an N+1 that eager-loading cannot fix because the count is not an association load.
